study.title: Origins of catalysis by computationally designed retroaldolase enzymes
study.enzyme_context: RA61 named study construct and five declared variants; two primary-amine comparators
study.source_scope: Complete six-page main article and nine-page author-linked SI. Original design files, exact sequence strings, coordinate files and assay specimens are not acquired.
study.development_exposure: Published outcomes selected for source annotation; not an unseen evaluation or prospective design cohort.

question: Which designed catalytic components have discriminating experimental contrasts, and what do those contrasts identify?

qualification.permitted_result: Named RA61 substitutions at designed water-contact positions increase the reported initial-rate second-order endpoint. Substrate-interaction and lysine-pKa contributions remain author estimates with explicit comparator and model dependencies.
qualification.scope_limit: Within-study declared RA61 backgrounds support source annotation despite absent exact sequences. No exact sequence, specimen, protein admission, mechanism compilation or independent validation follows.

downstream_catalytic_labels.null_semantics: Unestablished, not a negative label; no runtime enforcement is implemented.

selection.included: All six Table4 rows and all six Table5 cells, with the repeated RA61 full-substrate value stored once; RA61 pH-rate/pH-binding context and RA61 TableS1 model sensitivity.
selection.excluded: Other designs, the full Table3 amine series, raw-curve digitization/refitting, new structural measurements and exact enantiomer rates. Product-binding caveat retained only to bound the initial-rate endpoint.
selection.counting_rule: Table4 and Table5 share one RA61/full-substrate context, so twelve printed cells give eleven distinct stored contexts. Table1 repeats RA61 0.49; no extra experiment is counted. Derived ratios and model estimates are not observations.
selection.rationale: RA61 is the source-selected most active reported design. Its component contrasts do not estimate typical design behavior or a success rate.

sources.inspection: Complete text and visual pages1-6; Tables1/2/4/5, Figures1/2 and endpoint-defining Methods.

sources.inspection: Complete text; visual source figures/captions and TableS1, especially pages3/5/6/9. No complete amino-acid sequence is supplied.

assays.endpoint: Observed second-order initial-rate retroaldol endpoint from naphthaldehyde fluorescence, under subsaturating conditions before the first turnover.
assays.model: v0 = (kcat/KM)obs * [E] * [S] for enzyme; kobs * [amine] * [S] for solution catalysts
assays.source_locator: PMC2841948:article-PDF:pages1-3:Conditions for Kinetic Studies; page6:Kinetic Assays and Nonenzymatic, Amine-Catalyzed Reactions
assays.limits: Reports the second-order endpoint through aldehyde formation (source steps1-3), not separate kcat, KM, a single elementary step, steps4-5 or generic full-cycle turnover. Rates were linear in substrate and catalyst over at least tenfold ranges.

assays.endpoint: Observed second-order retroaldol rate from acetone appearance measured by proton NMR.
assays.technique: 600MHz proton NMR with water suppression and internal acetone calibration
assays.model: First order in enzyme or amine and in substrate.
assays.limits: Different reporter and specified solvent additives from full-substrate fluorescence. No matched-solvent correction or microscopic rate equivalence established; DMSO is unstated in this paragraph, not asserted absent.

component_evidence.source_reported_result: All five mutant constructs have larger displayed (kcat/KM)obs than parent RA61. The author reports no significant pH-rate-profile change for the double mutant, without numeric curve data or a stated statistical test; equivalence is not inferred.
component_evidence.admissible_interpretation: The data do not demonstrate a beneficial contribution from the modeled Tyr78/Ser87 motif to the measured initial-rate endpoint; all assayed substitutions increase that endpoint.
author_alternatives: Predicted interactions do not facilitate the measured reaction.
Mutations may improve bulk-solvent access; explicitly untested.

component_evidence.admissible_interpretation: Relative reactivity supports the author estimate of an extra contribution associated with the full substrate beyond intrinsic amine-catalyzed reactivity. It does not isolate individual pocket contacts, desolvation, affinity, preorganization or transition-state geometry.
assumptions: Solution amines reasonably control the intrinsic reactivity difference.
Cross-readout and solvent differences do not dominate the contrast.
The minimal substrate retains a hydroxybutanone scaffold and methyl groups capable of binding; this is not a no-binding baseline.
Changing substrate also changes size, stereochemistry, products and potentially the limiting transition state; no pure contact-deletion perturbation is supplied.
component_evidence.design_intent: Interactions with the naphthyl substrate surface (Figure2C), distinct from the pocket intended to lower Lys176 pKa (Figure2A).

source_reported_pKa.uncertainty_type: approximate author error estimate; not a stated SD or CI

component_evidence.residue_assignment: The authors attribute the compatible pH-rate and pH-binding profiles most simply to active-site lysine ionization under their mechanism model; no new matched Lys-replacement assay or direct residue-specific titration is provided.

source_reported_pKa_contribution.assumption: Enzymatic and solution-amine Bronsted values are similar.

component_evidence.sensitivity_scope: RA61 row of SI TableS1; alternative model assumptions, not a confidence interval or measured mutation effects.

reference_pKa.species: lysine side chain reference represented by primary alkylamine in solution
reference_pKa.source_locator: PMC2841948:article-PDF:page3:Rate Acceleration Relative to Lysine Side Chain in Solution; PMC2841948:SI-PDF:page9:TableS1 text
reference_pKa.scope: Source reference/model baseline; not a measured pKa of the RA61 protein or a new free-lysine experiment.

component_evidence.model_formula_scope: SI page9 equations expressed as enzyme/reference second-order rate ratio at a common pH. Source-reported approximate fold estimates are retained, not replaced by recalculation or promoted to direct measurements. Displayed inputs do not reproduce every printed TableS1 integer exactly; retain the source estimates without numerical repair, inferred hidden precision or an unverified rounding explanation.

source_limitations: The lysine-necessity statement on main page3 cites Jiang2008 Ref7; the acquired 2010 main/SI supplies no new matched catalytic-Lys replacement assay. This does not assert absence in the unacquired 2008 study.

The RA61 model contains Tyr78/Ser87 water contacts. Main Figure2 explicitly calls it a design model; the experimental RA61 structure lacks bound ligand and does not establish substrate orientation or the designed water position. No coordinate-derived measurement is added.
Table4 has no row-specific SD, replicate count or detection limit. Table1 says SD less than20% over multiple assays/protein preparations; that statement is not assigned to every Table4/5 row.

Methods report protein preparation and pH-stability controls but do not provide mutant-specific fold equivalence, active-fraction, structural or matched affinity controls. A substitution effect cannot be isolated to one chemical contribution.
Main prose summarizes single-mutant increases as2-3fold; Table4 has1.6 for S87A and3.7 for S87G. The numerical table entries are retained without silently narrowing them to the prose range.

No beneficial motif effect at the observed initial-rate endpoint is not proof that water is absent or unnecessary in every catalytic step. Bulk-solvent access is an untested author explanation, and compensating mutation effects remain possible.

No design hit-rate denominator, new experimental observation by this project, independent human review, evidence-tier promotion, mechanistic role transfer, or productive-geometry tolerance is supplied.

cross_case_comparison.relation: A designed catalytic-component label needs endpoint-specific evidence: substitution sensitivity, apparent ionization, and model-derived substrate effects are different kinds of support.
cross_case_comparison.use: RA95.5-5 K210M and its parent illustrate parameter-dependent substitution effects; KE59 retains indirect pH evidence. They contextualize RA61 evidence types without claiming equal conditions, homologous sites, common exact constructs or a cross-study activity ranking. Existing packets are unchanged; no sequence strings copied.

reconsideration.bespoke_code: No new runtime or validator. Component roles, source-local positions, assay identity, missingness, observations and model assumptions fit additive data.
reconsideration.reuse: Shared assay/construct/provenance and source-reported-versus-derived ratio concepts reused; RA61 0.49 stored once across repeated table contexts; prior accepted packets linked by exact hash/pointer. No measured speedup claimed.
reconsideration.incumbent_value: The authors already identify the component limitations. The reusable relation keeps designed roles separate from observed mutation effects and comparator/model estimates, preventing the roughly500-fold substrate estimate from becoming affinity or a precise geometric constraint. No superiority to a competent literature reader is claimed.

initial_rate_boundary.source_observation: Naphthaldehyde fluorescence decreases on incubation with enzyme, and increasing enzyme concentration increases curvature of progress traces.
initial_rate_boundary.author_model: Off-pathway enzyme-product iminium binding reduces free enzyme and fluorescent free product; apparent burst behavior need not report the later reaction steps.

product_binding_estimate.assumptions: Assumes bound product has zero fluorescence; binding saturation was not reached.

initial_rate_boundary.admissible_use: Motivates the initial-rate measurement regime. Product-binding estimates are not substrate KM, a catalytic-intermediate affinity or an elementary-step rate.
